obligations.obligation: Closed positive (1,1) currents have uniform local trace growth Cr^(2n-2) by the actually read Lelong mass formula and its proof.
Hausdorff-null ball covers and coefficient domination prove the new current-null corollary; no assertion is made for arbitrary positive nonclosed currents.
The binary Cantor covers give Hausdorff dimension zero separately for K and K times K.
The disc Green kernel has the book normalization ddc g=sigma, is nonpositive and vanishes uniformly near the boundary.
Cantor interval mass forces g=-infinity on every point of K; outside K the integral is finite harmonic and smooth.
Nonatomic sigma gives zero Lelong number at every point.
The maximum suppresses a pole branch off the joint pole set and is locally Lipschitz there.
The soft maximum of two pluriharmonic functions has Hessian rank at most one; bounded decreasing BT convergence gives zero square.
Truncations are continuous and their top-degree measure is supported on the compact triple-equality level Q_L.
Local CLN gives finite mass; compact-support bounded integration by parts makes the mass independent of L.
The negative bounded truncation and a small strictly psh quadratic give a nonempty relatively compact comparison set and strictly positive common mass.
Deep level sets approach K and hence Q_L approaches the joint pole set.
The cutoff is constant near all poles; cross derivative terms are bounded on compact support where h is locally Lipschitz, giving a global finite curvature lower bound.
Small positive scaling gives strict Kähler curvature and a genuine normalized global potential with exactly the joint pole set.
Bounded global truncations have total mass A by closed-background Stokes.
The localized positive measures have mass t^2 M, approach S and are dominated by the global truncation measures; a common weak subsequence retains this positive mass on S.
Truncations equal the locally bounded potential eventually off S, identifying the off-pole weak limit with the non-pluripolar measure.
The strict current lower bound gives positive mass, while polar concentration gives a strict deficit from A; no exact value of M is asserted.
Closed-background bounded-equivalence mass invariance identifies both singularity volumes; the complete used ordinary-envelope-volumes proof preserves them and gives a normalized nonzero model.
The ordered model volume comparison with zero is A minus that preserved volume, and both models lie in a common positive lower-volume sector.
The model lies above the original potential and below zero, so its pole set is contained in the zero-dimensional joint set.
For a smooth compact surface modification, the exceptional locus consists of finitely many curves contracted to finitely many points; away from these fibers the map is an isomorphism.
Arbitrary-pole closedness gives a closed positive polar current on every modification; the Hausdorff estimate makes it vanish off the exceptional curves.
The actually checked analytic support theorem reduces that current to a positive finite sum of exceptional curve currents.
The bound b_i <= generic Lelong number uses positivity after a smooth correction; it does not assert an unchecked exact divisorial identity for arbitrary unbounded potentials.
Outside the joint pole set the original potential is locally bounded, forcing zero exceptional coefficient.
At each remaining generic exceptional point the first coordinate is a positive power of a normal coordinate times a unit; a holomorphic root absorbs the unit.
One-variable circular means give multiplicity times the original zero Lelong number; the lower comparison by t g forces every exceptional coefficient to vanish.
Zero point Lelong numbers and Skoda integrability at every positive weight give trivial multiplier ideals and zero ideal envelope, so the nonzero ordinary model is nonideal.
Every modification has zero first polar current, independent of all Gauduchon choices; the analytic zero model has pseudodistance zero to the nonideal model.
The specific all-modifications first-polar candidate fails separation and exact ideal analytic closure; the 23 full formal questions and 18 supplemental directions remain open at their stated scope.
